In this way too he wisely, and with fitting precision, makes evident [?] that what is revealed cannot fail to come to pass.
And great fear fell.

The "great fear" may be meant as something that will actually and perceptibly happen then, when these things come to pass, or it may be meant in some other sense. But there is no need to busy ourselves over this, since either way salvation is provided, in a manner pleasing to God, to the souls of those who love to stay watchful.
And they went up to heaven in the cloud.

A cloud is always a servant of divine works. Sometimes it surrounds them, as in "Cloud and darkness are round about him"; sometimes it carries them, as in other places and indeed here as well. The cloud gets its name from the clouds that have shed what is thick and watery. These clouds naturally take their substance from vapour rising off moist matter as it evaporates. Since, then, the cloud owes its existence to such clouds, one sees in it a certain obscurity together with a certain brightness, which is produced by the sun's rays falling on it and being reflected. That is why it always accompanies divine revelations. It hints that divine things are neither wholly hidden from us nor offered entirely openly, but that something like the radiance of unmixed light is trained to show itself under concealment. In just this sense the cloud now serves the prophets' ascent to heaven. And so, as is customary with such things, it is used with the article: for he says they went up "in the cloud". This is how the mystical teaching is conveyed, since articles, as we noted a little earlier, bring to mind something already known. Let this be our account of the cloud. In the plain sense of the word, it is called a cloud because it takes its substance from a cloud that has shaken off all that is thick and watery. For moist vapour forms clouds, and once this has been shaken out as rain, as though it had been digested, what remains undigested goes to form the cloud. Because of its thinness and transparency, [?] the light of the sun lingers in it, so that it is like a cloud lit up and shining.
In that day there was a great earthquake.

It is made clear that these things will happen both perceptibly and in a spiritual sense to be grasped by contemplation, and neither is to be rejected. For we take the earthquake, spiritually understood, to signify the removal of what is shaken to what is firm and secure. The fall of a tenth of the city is the fall of impiety, of those who were not chastened even by the destruction of the slain, since the rest are to be saved. For the seven thousand who are killed appear to signify those who cling to the seven-day period of this present life and do not wait for the eighth day of the resurrection. These are also put to death with the eternal death of punishment in Gehenna. For this perceptible world, having no place any longer in that pure age, cannot linger on [?]. Hence the rest rightly sent up thanksgiving to God, giving glory to the God of heaven. For earthly things, that is, things akin to corruption, will no longer be at work, so as to need divine oversight [?]. The second woe has passed. The third is coming, in which the seventh angel will sound his trumpet.
And a tenth of the city fell.

What is he hinting at by this? Is it that the part of the world which at that time seems complete, whether in virtue or in vice, and which has neither been chastened by the punishment of those who perished nor turned to what truly is, will be handed over to eternal condemnation?
And names were killed in the earthquake.

He has used a rather peculiar way of speaking. For it was not the names that were killed. How could they be, since names belong to the category of accidents? Accidents come to be and pass away without the destruction of their subject, as those skilled in these matters show. Rather, the saying must be understood of the destruction of those to whom the names had been given. For a name is not given to nothing, and it was they who were subjected to destruction.
On the seventh trumpet, and on the saints who sing praise to God at the coming judgment.

And the seventh angel sounded his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying, "The kingdom of the world has come, and that of our Lord Jesus Christ, and he will reign for ever and ever." And the twenty-four elders who sit on their thrones before the throne of God fell on their faces and worshipped God, saying, "We give you thanks, Lord God Almighty, who are and who were, because you have taken your great power and begun to reign. The nations raged, and your wrath has come, and the time for the dead to be judged, and for rewarding your servants the prophets and the saints and those who fear your name, both small and great, and for destroying those who destroy the earth."

The sounding of the seventh angel's trumpet presents what belongs to the third woe: loud voices ringing out in heaven and making a declaration. For that is what "saying" means, as we have said before. What, then, does "the kingdom has come" signify? God never began, and never ceases, to reign over things visible and invisible, over all things that can be conceived and those that cannot (for human understanding does not grasp them all). Rather, without beginning and without end, he is Lord and Master of all. But worldly rule and kingdom have at times shown themselves insubordinate to him, puffed up by their own vanities, and from this a dreamlike glory came upon this mortal world, ending in corruption. So when those who reign and play the tyrant on earth, not in truth but as in a mirror and a phantom, are brought down and come to an end, he who alone is truly God and King is said to rule and reign for ever, with a power and authority that passes to no successor.
And the twenty-four elders.

Who these twenty-four are has already been considered. So here too he says that both the holy angels and those who have lived the angelic life in this world send up thanksgiving to the Almighty, to whom belong "who is" and "who was". "Who is" fits the Holy Trinity, as was said before, and so does "who was". Even if "who is" is said chiefly of the Father and "who was" of the Son, still no one who has resolved to judge divine things wisely and in a manner worthy of God would doubt that both are said of all three hypostases. For apart from the properties that distinguish the hypostases, everything else applies without reservation to the three persons. So the elders' thanksgiving is offered to the Holy Trinity, both to all in common and to each individually. The great power has been taken through true knowledge, as the shadows pass away. The kingdom which he possessed as God from the beginning he gave to human beings; that is why it is said, "By me kings reign, and tyrants rule the earth." This kingdom he who became man for our sake deigned to receive, above all as man. When this happened and the earthly kingdom perished, the nations were naturally enraged, since their dominion had been overthrown. By "nations" he means the bands of demons and the ranks of unbelieving men: the demons were deprived of their worship, and so were the nations, as by a new and foreign teaching [?]. Having long been patient, at the end he brought judgment, a judgment worthy both of divine forbearance and of their hardness and ingratitude.
They fell on their faces.
Falling can also mean simply sitting or lying down. So that this would not be supposed, he added "on their faces", which is the honour owed to a master by those beneath him.
And your wrath has come.

He says: Having been very patient with people of old, since they gained nothing from your kindness, you have now come at the appointed time. By "the time of the dead" he means the time of the universal resurrection, in which each will be given the fitting recompense. By the prophets, the saints and those who fear God he means the three ranks of those who bear fruit a hundredfold, sixtyfold and thirtyfold. The apostles are granted the first lot and a seat on the twelve thrones, and likewise the prophets, especially those who were subjected to punishment by kings raging against them. "Small and great": the small are those less holy, the great those who excel more in holiness. Fear is of two kinds: one is preparatory, the other perfecting. The preparatory kind belongs to those who have not yet received acquittal; the perfecting kind belongs to those already taken up by God, who always fear lest anything be lacking in them, a fear naturally present in those who love intensely. So I think it should not be rejected that "those who fear" are ranked below "the saints". The small are held by fear in the proper sense, while the great have confidence, as has been said, and yet fear accompanies their confidence too. Both, then, have fear, on account of the recompense and reward that match the worth of the lives they have lived. For the great, the fear is this very thing: that they do not trust themselves to be without defect. For the small, it is while they hope without hesitation to be saved [?]. And [he will destroy the destroyers] because they subjected the servants of God to cruel evils, and by their other outrageous deeds defiled and corrupted the earth.
On the earlier persecutions of the Church, and on those in the time of the Antichrist.
And the temple in heaven was opened, and the ark of the Lord's covenant was seen in his temple. And there were lightnings and voices and thunders and great hail.

After the angels, and those who have lived like the angels, give glory in thanksgiving, he says that heaven was opened and the ark of the covenant was seen. By "heaven" he means knowledge beyond the human, in which are also stored up "what eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the human heart, what God has prepared for those who love him." In this heaven of knowledge the ark of the covenant was also seen. What does the vision mean to show by it? At that earlier time Moses was told that the things set before him were symbols and did not hold the reality itself: "See," it says, "that you make everything according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain." In the same way the vision now teaches that we should not stop at the things that are seen. Instead it lifts our knowledge to a matching heavenly height. When the ark of the covenant was shown to Moses, lightnings and thunders came first on the mountain where it pleased God to reveal these things, and they made the mountain untouchable for irrational and beastlike creatures. So here too, when the ark is shown, the things proper to this vision follow.
And there were lightnings.

This is the third woe, which was prepared for sinners. In the same way, the sight of the good things laid up for the saints was prepared for them. Until now these good things were unknown to human beings, but they have come to be known through the opening of God's temple in heaven. The Savior also speaks of them at the mystical supper: "From now on I will not drink of this fruit of this vine until I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father." For then those who have lived well will be found worthy of the return to life, and they will obtain the good things laid up for the holy in the kingdom of the Father.

And a great sign was seen in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and on her head crowns of twelve stars. She was with child, and she cried out in labor, in anguish to give birth.

A woman found worthy of such glory. We have already said that he gives the name "heaven" to thoughts that rise above mortal nature. Some people apply their knowledge to what is shown as though they had hit the mark, and in their ignorance they think they can insist on it. That belongs to a bold and self-willed mind. But to share with others, without insisting on it, what one has been found worthy to receive in proportion to one's own purification belongs to a fair and moderate man. Therefore we will set out what we have learned from those before us about the matters at hand, and leave each reader to choose which view to accept. Some, then, have taken this woman to be the Mother of the Lord. Shortly before, the vision went through the matters concerning the Antichrist, and words were spoken about his coming and about Satan putting him forward. Satan is eager to use deceit to persuade those already given over to Christ to turn back and desert to him. From the very beginning of the Lord's incarnation Satan wickedly attacked people, and he set out to build his deception by imitating these things. He did so above all among the Hebrews, who apply the prophecies about Christ to that man rather than to Christ. So the vision corrects this deception by setting forth the Lord's dispensation for our sake as already accomplished, and by showing that no other could ever rival it. That is why it describes the mother as in heaven and not on earth: she is pure and freed from earthly things, equal to the angels. Yet although she so far surpassed others in purity, she shared the same human dough as we do. For what does David say about the Lord's conception? "He will come down like rain upon a fleece, and like a drop falling upon the earth." Here he calls the holy Mother of the Lord "earth," because she is of one substance with us who are earthly. As for Eutyches' unholy teaching about the Theotokos and the Lord's taking flesh, let it be thrown somewhere outside the sacred precincts. Habakkuk is able to explain why she is clothed with the sun and has the moon as a footstool, when he says, "The sun was lifted up, and the moon stood in its order." By the sun he means Christ the Savior, the Sun of righteousness, exalted and raised on high by the preaching of the gospel. By the moon he means the synagogue of the Jews, which received no further increase. For after Christ's appearing it no longer gained additions from the nations through proselytes. Rather, it has even been diminished as Jews go over to the Christians. We can also understand being clothed with the sun as the holy Virgin being covered by the spiritual Sun, that is, by Christ. And we can understand the moon as the worship and way of life under the law, which has been brought low and has become far less than it was, outshone [?] by the beacon of the gospel. Another reason is that the law and its commands are illumined by Christ the Sun, just as the moon is lit by the visible sun. Perhaps it would have been more consistent with the meaning to say, not that the woman was clothed with the sun, but that she clothed the sun she carried in her womb. But the vision wanted to show that even while he was carried in the womb, the Lord surpassed both his own mother and all creation. So it said that he covered his mother as with a garment. This agrees with what Gabriel said to the Virgin: "The power of the Most High will overshadow you." For to cover someone as with a garment is the same as to overshadow them.

Others again, among them Saint Methodius of Patara, apply the vision to the holy Church. They think these things do not fit the Lord's birth, since the Lord had been born long before. The Church, then, is clothed with the Sun of righteousness and with the light of the law, which is the night-shining moon. The law is likened to the moon because it gave a faint gleam, I mean the light of the knowledge of God, to a whole world held in darkness as regards true worship. And since it changes along with worldly life, it has been given its place under the Church's feet. The crown on her head is adorned with twelve stars: plainly this is Christ's Church with the apostles. The same Methodius also says that, since the moon governs moist substance, which is figuratively called the sea, it signifies holy baptism, which destroys demons but saves people of good will. So he says that the woman must be understood as the Church, not as the holy Virgin giving birth to Christ. For this mystery of the incarnation had been accomplished long before, and John is shown knowledge of things to come, not of things that have already happened. The Church, then, the new Zion, is in labor, to use the words of the divine Paul. She groans as she gives birth to those who are being redeemed, until Christ is formed in them. She fears the dragon until she escapes his schemes and gives birth to Christ in each person, as he is spiritually formed in each one. That is why she swells and labors until Christ is born and formed in us, so that each person is born to share in Christ.
And on her head crowns.

The words "under her feet" have been explained according to those who take the woman in heaven to be the Mother of God. About the crown on her head they say that the Virgin Mary is crowned by the twelve apostles who preach Christ. For the glory of Christ as he is preached shows what kind of glory belongs to the one who bore him. As for the woman with child crying out in labor and in anguish over the birth, he says that Amos [?], Isaiah, resolves this when he says: "Before she who was in labor gave birth, and before the pain of her labor came, she escaped and bore a male child." Gregory of Nyssa too, in the thirteenth homily of his commentary on the Song of Songs, says of the Lord: "The conception was without union, the childbirth undefiled, without pain and without labor pangs." But Revelation presents the woman in labor as crying out and in anguish over the birth, while the prophet and the divine father say nothing of the kind. So we will say that both things happened to the Virgin. She did cry out, and she was in distress, suspecting that her betrothed would bring a charge of adultery against her. The Gospel also indicates this when it says that he planned to divorce her secretly. But when a divine angel freed her from this suspicion by confirming that the conception was from the Holy Spirit, then she too escaped all the trouble that pained her. And if the Gospel does not show anything of this kind about the Virgin, such as that she was in anguish over the pregnancy, that is no objection. Otherwise you will also say that Moses told a false story about himself. When he saw himself pressed by the Egyptians at the Red Sea, he endured in silence and prayed in secret, yet he heard from God: "Why do you cry out to me?"

And another sign was seen in heaven: behold, a great red dragon, with seven heads and ten horns, and seven diadems on his heads. His tail drags away a third of the stars of heaven, and he threw them down to the earth.

He calls Satan a dragon because he is crooked. Isaiah also calls him this when he speaks of "the dragon, the crooked serpent." He is red because he is bloodthirsty and wrathful. Or he is red because angelic substance is fiery. For he has not been changed in his angelic substance, only in his will, and it was through his will that he fell. Whoever says that "heaven" here means the air misses the mark. For how could he have fallen from the air when, to use Paul's words, he holds authority in it as "the ruler," he says, "of the darkness of this air"? His heads are his more wicked powers, which are opposed to the workings of the Spirit. Or they are the spirits that, as the Gospel says, settle in the house that has been swept. Or they are the seven evils that Solomon says are in the heart of the enemy.

In keeping with what was said at the beginning, the vision now also means to tell more fully the things concerning the Antichrist. So it starts from the Lord's conception and birth. In rivalry with these, the common enemy of us all, Satan, puts forward the Antichrist. Through the resemblance he steals away some of the less genuine believers and those who listen too carelessly to the prophecies about Christ. So the vision has set out to present the things concerning the Antichrist starting, as it were, from the Lord's birth. But it also sets out another, older beginning: Satan's fall from heaven, which it will present more clearly in the following vision. Its present aim is to establish this point. The one who will come forward as a rival to the incarnation of the true Christ has always, from the beginning, [?] dared to set himself against those above him, and he fell from what he had, together with his whole phalanx and band. At the Lord's coming he also attempted his usual deeds: at the birth through Herod, and in the rest of the dispensation through the Pharisees [?] who came after. In those cases he was defeated in shame. In the same way, at the coming of the Antichrist, though he contrives many deceptions, he will nevertheless be handed over with his whole army to the eternal fire. By setting these things out in advance the vision has made us secure, and it has left without excuse those who are caught after this warning. Now that we have looked at these things in summary, let us go on to the details more fully.
And ten horns.

The horn signifies power and glory. It signifies power in David: "And I will break all [the horns] of sinners, and the horn of the righteous shall be exalted." It signifies glory where Hannah says, "My horn was exalted in my God." There are ten horns for one of two reasons. They may be the transgressions set against the ten commandments of the law, the undertakings that bring the satanic apostasy to completion. For ten is the first perfect number after the unit, and it generates perfection. Or they may be the divisions of the kingdom, which bring him adornment, since he delights in dissensions. The seven diadems on his heads are equal in number to the heads. This is because those who win the victory over demonic workings carry off their crowns from the very place where they won with toil and sweat. The great Methodius also speaks of these things, word for word: "The great red dragon, the seven-headed one who drags away a third of the stars, who stands lying in wait to devour the child of the woman in labor, is the devil." And further on: "But he misses and fails to take his prey, because those who are born again are caught up on high."
And his tail drags away a third of the stars.

The third part of the stars is the name given to those who went astray about one member of the Trinity, such as Arius and Macedonius. The wilderness where the Church comes and is fed is the wilderness that is empty of evils and barren of corruption. The tail dragging away a third of the stars can also be understood in another way. We think two things are shown here. The first is his earlier fall from heaven, together with the angels who rebelled with him, through his last movement, which was envy. That is what the tail is. For first pride drew him toward envy, and it dashed these angels down to the earth. The second is the movement of his tail after his head was crushed by the Lord's disciples, who received from the Lord "authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the evil power." This later movement of the tail, his last, brought down from heavenly thinking those who were unstable. They are figuratively called stars because of the brightness they received in baptism. Daniel prophesied in the same way about Antiochus, who would be a type of the Antichrist.
And he threw them down to the earth.

For it brought down with itself a large share of the angels, having persuaded them to rebel with it against God. It made the heavenly into earthly beings, and those who were bright as stars into darkness.

And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child. And she bore a son, a male, who is to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron. And her child was caught up to God and to his throne. And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there they may nourish her for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
The dragon stands plotting treacherously against the child. This shows that he took great pains to prepare hardships for the one who was born, and what these were has been told.
And her child was caught up to God.

The venomous dragon lay in wait and spurred Herod on to kill the infants in Bethlehem, intending to do away with Christ among them. But by God's providence the Father warned Joseph to take the child and his mother and flee to Egypt, because Herod was going to seek the child's life. So the child escaped the plot. Since this happened by the Father's providence through the divine warning, the vision describes the child's bodily rescue as a "catching up," saying "to God and to his throne." It is as if to say that the child's safety was arranged by divine providence and lordship. For that is what the throne is meant to show.
And the woman fled into the wilderness.

Those who take the woman to mean the Church have explained the catching up of the child to God and to his throne in two ways. The first is God's rescue of the righteous from temptations here and now, as in the promise "Six times he will deliver you from distress," and "He will not let us be tempted beyond what we can bear, but with the temptation he will also provide the way out." The second is the final rescue at the restoration, when the friends of God will be caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air and will be with the angelic powers at the throne of God. The woman's flight into the wilderness means the flight of the elect. At the coming of the Antichrist, which the devil brings about, the foremost members of the Church will flee, escaping from civic turmoil and worldly pleasures. They will flee to where they are used to withdrawing in affliction, as it is said, "Lord, in affliction we remembered you." And remembrance comes through self-control: "For everyone," says Paul, "who competes exercises self-control in all things." So at that time the members of the Church will withdraw into the wilderness, a wilderness empty of all pleasure and vice but rich in every virtue and love of God, and there they will escape the assaults of the demons. It is likely too that a literal wilderness will save those who hide themselves in mountains and caves and holes in the ground from the plotting of the apostate, as happened earlier to the martyrs of Christ. The apostasy will last three and a half years, for that is the span of time that the one thousand two hundred and sixty days make up. During it, those who contend with endurance will receive the victor's crown from God, the good judge of the contest, who knows how to give rewards worthy of the labors.

The woman fled with the child. The mother escaped into a wilderness empty of every godly work. For there God had set apart a place for her to be nourished for one thousand two hundred and sixty days, the span of Herod's life, as the holy Gospel also records.

You reject the view that the woman is rightly taken to mean the Lord's mother and his dispensation, and you take her as the Church instead. Your reason is that these things happened long ago, while the Revelation reveals things to come, not things that have already happened. Then how is it that you yourself, as if you had forgotten, bring up the devil's fall at the beginning?
On the war that took place between the holy angels and the evil powers, and on the fall of the dragon.

And war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back, but they did not prevail, and there was no longer any place for them in heaven. And the great dragon was thrown down, that ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.

The one who gives the revelation keeps moving back, step by step, to a beginning older than the one already stated. He touched on part of this earlier, when he was taking us through the events concerning the Antichrist. The first beginning of the things concerning the Antichrist is his fall from heaven. That is why the Lord says, "I was watching Satan fall from heaven like lightning." What does he mean by this? Is he saying that something which happened long ago took place only recently, in his own day? That is not how it should be understood. The Word of God, who is also God, was united in essence with the manhood and joined with it in the one hypostasis of Jesus Christ. According to his divine nature he was with God the Father eternally and never left him, and so he also saw the devil's fall. Some may ignorantly try to find fault with the saying because he did not use the past tense and say "I saw," but said "I was watching." They should know that divine things are always active, since they always exist. They are not subject to differences of time, so that they do not quietly slip into nonexistence through age. As the wise saying puts it, "Everything that grows old and aged is near to vanishing." Divine things are always active and continually enrich the present. So the Lord fittingly said "I was watching" and not "I saw." He who was present then as God is now, by the economy of salvation, joined into one indivisible hypostasis. Because of this perfect union he makes the divine attributes his own in his human body as well. That is why he does not hesitate to assign "I was watching" to his humanity too. So he says, in effect: since Satan's casting out from the heavenly places is in force, I give you authority to trample boldly and without effort on those who have long since been laid low.

Scripture calls it a war because Satan stiffened his neck against God, raising a hard and arrogant neck against him and rushing into rebellion. God bore his audacity with patience. The Archangel Gabriel, in subordination to the divine and blessed nature... For, as the saying goes, that nature neither has troubles nor causes them for others. To the One who is without beginning and has his being from no one, the [?] of an essence made from nothing does not belong. Only such an essence has been allotted changeability, because it came from nonbeing. Since it has passed from one state to another, it is also open to change. The divine essence is not: it is beyond essence and has neither beginning nor alteration. The created essence shows alteration in itself. What could be seen in the Ever-Existent that tends toward change? For this reason, since the divine is marked by its unchangeableness, the nature that comes after it took up the war. That nature came into being from nothing and found itself subject to change, and the Old Testament makes Michael known as its leader. Together with the spiritual host under him, Michael clashed in battle with the rebellious Satan and the demonic order with him. He won the victory over him and drove him out of his heavenly dwelling. This is what "there was no longer any place for him in heaven" means. And he was thrown down to the earth. Either he suffered this in a physical sense, or he was stripped of his angelic and heavenly rank and cast down into an earthly mind. Then, as though taking revenge on God for his fall, and unable to strike back at God himself, he tempts God's servants, human beings, thinking that in this way he wrongs their Master.

The war in heaven arose from the first arrogance and from envy of Adam. God himself did not take the field, for he stands above every created nature that he brought from nonbeing into being. That is why changeability always clings to such a nature. He himself is the truly blessed nature, lacking nothing whatsoever. If one may dare say it, his is a self-grounded nature, and so it does not admit of "whence" [?] or "of what kind." The war was taken up by the angelic essence that comes after him, which the divine Michael has been appointed to lead. It did so long ago at the beginning, and more completely at the passion of Christ. That is why Christ himself says, "Now the ruler of this world has been judged," meaning fully condemned. The divine Paul also says that the devil rules the air of the world. The chief commander Michael would not tolerate the devil's arrogance. Long ago he hurled him by force of arms from his own dwelling. As Ezekiel says, the cherub drove him out from among the fiery stones, meaning the angelic orders, because iniquities were found in him. Then again, at the coming of Christ, as has been said, the angels who ministered to the Lord himself sent him away like a disgraced slave after his temptations of the Lord. So the devil fell more completely.

This is confirmed by the tradition of the fathers and by Papias, the successor of John the Evangelist, to whom the present Apocalypse also belongs. On this very passage Papias speaks about the war in these words: "Their battle line came to nothing," meaning their attempt at war, "for the great dragon was thrown down, the ancient serpent, who is called Satan and the devil, and he was thrown down to the earth, he and his angels." He has two names: he is called both Satan and the devil. Some say that this casting out of the devil took place after Christ's baptism and temptation, when Christ had said to him, "Go away, Satan." This seems to fit very well with what has been said about the Theotokos. He is called by two names. He is "Satan" because he is the adversary of the Master. He is "devil" because he slanders God to human beings, as he did to Adam, and slanders the virtues and those who practice them.

It should be understood that the devil's fall after the Lord's crucifixion was not a change of place. He himself admitted this to the divine Antony [?], saying, "The swords of the enemy have utterly failed." His fall is the setting aside of their wicked works, together with the loss of his heavenly rule, as has been said, more completely. The holy martyr Justin also says that after Christ's coming and the sentence of Gehenna passed on him, the devil became especially blasphemous, though before he had not blasphemed God so shamelessly. That is why it was aptly said of him, "His heart is as hard as stone," because his wickedness does not yield. If the expectation of punishment made him more wicked, how could he, or those who carry out his evils, be washed clean of the filth of sin by burning in Gehenna while being punished? And if this does not happen, how will their punishment come to an end, as the vain-minded claim? Let them consider this, if for no other reason, then at least because the gifts of God are irrevocable, and one of these gifts is memory. The soul has been stained in human memory with a dye that cannot be washed out and a permanence that does not fade. Memory lies on it constantly and sets before it the gloom of its fall. How will it not consume the soul more painfully than fire? For what does the saying say? "A thought that will not leave is a wasting of the heart." And if [?] ... blessed are the sinners, released by nonexistence from unspeakable pains. But since they are raised to a life that cannot be dissolved, what hope is left for them?

And I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying: "Now the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God have come, and the authority of his Christ, for the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night. And they conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives even to death. Therefore rejoice, you heavens, and you who dwell in them! Woe to the earth and the sea, for the devil has come down to you in great fury, because he knows that his time is short."

He was granted the ascent to heaven, and from there he watched the war and the victory of the divine angels over Satan, the devil. He says that he also heard a voice saying. As I have often noted, "saying" is used here in the sense of "making known." Making what known? The joy the angels felt at the victory over Satan, the devil. They branded him with these two names, matching the number of his activities. For he opposes every good, and he has never stopped slandering from the beginning, as already said. So they sing a joyful song over his defeat and expulsion. A believer has no fellowship or share with an unbeliever. And what is the song? "Now the salvation and the kingdom and the power of God have come." His power and authority, and that of his Christ, have shone out most clearly. With his help the accuser of our brothers has been defeated and has gone away from us. The word "now" is not used here to mean something recent. It means what is complete, sure, beyond doubt, and in keeping with the beginning. For beginnings are proved by their ends. Otherwise a thing could not even be called a beginning. What would it be the beginning of, if it did not bring an end?
Of our brothers.

Angels call human beings brothers in imitation of their own Master. For he himself says through the prophet, "I will declare your name to my brothers." And he said in person to Mary Magdalene, "Go to my brothers and tell them."
Day and night.

He says the accuser builds up his accusation against our brothers day and night. This shows how persistent and unceasing the evil one's abuse of us is. What else would he be eager for? Because his offense was so great, his very frenzy has become his name.
For he is always slandering: God to human beings, as he did to Adam through the serpent, and human beings to God, as he did with Job of Uz.
And they conquered him by the blood of the Lamb.

They conquered him by repelling him in war with the same weapons he had used when he insolently attacked the friends of God. So he went away and was stripped of his rank. He no longer had room to stand before God and accuse human beings, as he did in the case of Job. The martyrs conquered the one who seemed invincible, so invincible that he even dared to rise against God. They did so with the blood of the Lamb as their ally. How? Christ gave his blood not for himself but for us. The Passover lamb in the Old Testament was a type of this: it was slaughtered not for itself but for the safety of the Hebrews, so that the destroyer would not enter their houses and bring death on the firstborn. In the same way, the martyrs of Christ, in zeal for the slaughter of their own Master, chose to imitate the Master's passion over their own life and breath. Once this happened, the outcome gives cause for rejoicing to those freed from Satan's bitter company. Here too one should note the tense, which assigns future events to the past. Who does not know that the things announced here give knowledge not of the past but of the future, I mean of how things will unfold at the end of the age? It occurred to me to say this because some have tried to use the difference in tense to separate the woman and her male child [?] from the interpretation that refers to the Lord's mother. And by the word of their testimony.
By "word" he means their zeal for, and imitation of, the testimony the Lord bore through the cross.
Therefore rejoice, you heavens.

The angels show the joy they felt at Satan's overthrow and sing a victory song to God. They say: "Now salvation has come, and the kingdom has shone forth, and the authority of God's power, showing that he is almighty. For with his help we have conquered the enemy."
Woe to the earth and the sea.

The woe is not addressed to the senseless creation. It is addressed to those who think earthly thoughts and are dust, and who, as it is written, "are unstable like the sea," driven and tossed about in the gamble of life. The common enemy wages war against these people and gets what he wants. But he will come down on those who are sober and reach up toward God not to harm them but even to benefit them. They are trained as if by a wrestling master, and their temptations make them more tested and proven. He says the devil will have greater fury because he reckons how little time remains to him after his fall. For how long is the time since the devil's fall, whether counted from the beginning or from Christ's coming, when it is measured against the endless ages of his punishment? So, he says, having great fury, he will pursue the woman.
How the dragon never stops pursuing the Church.

And when the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child. But the woman was given the two wings of the great eagle, so that she could fly from the serpent into the wilderness, to her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time. Then the serpent poured water like a river from his mouth after the woman, to sweep her away with the flood. But the earth came to the woman's help: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had poured from his mouth. Then the dragon was enraged at the woman and went off to make war on the rest of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus.

Those who take the woman to be the Church explain her persecution this way. After his baptism Christ wrestled with the devil, and the devil saw that he had been defeated. In the same way he armed himself against Christ's disciples, the apostles, and was put to shame, because through death for Christ's sake they found life. He saw himself condemned, like the serpent, to the earth and to eat earth, meaning the earthly-minded, who have no share in the heavenly rebirth and way of life. Then, it says, he began once more to persecute the Church. From her comes the male people of the Lord. This people has nothing effeminate about it, none of the things that by nature slacken and soften a person through the pleasures of this life. From the beginning it has been braced by love for God and neighbor. It received from God the two wings of the great eagle, which make it light and force it to rise aloft. The eagle is the one who "rides upon the cherubim and flies," as David, the ancestor of God, has it. What else would anyone think the wings are but God's two covenants with us, the old and the new? These wings lift those who use them genuinely high up and carry them into the wilderness, away from every soft and watery pleasure. They do this always, but especially at the coming of the Antichrist, who will rule for the time already mentioned, three and a half years. During that time the faithful will also flee and hide in the literal wilderness, in mountains and caves and holes in the ground.

Another interpretation. Those who have taken the woman to be the Lord's mother say that this passage goes back over what has already been said. It does not say that the dragon pursued the woman immediately after he saw that he had been thrown down to the earth. Rather, when the dragon saw what evils he was in, and that he had fallen from his angelic rank, he became extremely bitter against human beings. He pursued the woman who gave birth to the Savior of humankind in order to destroy her, because he knew that the child to be born of her would be the Savior of humankind. He could not bear such a reversal: he himself had fallen from heaven, while human beings would rise up to heaven through virtue by the loving power and divine authority of the one to be born of her. So, as far as it lay in his power, he never stopped contriving every kind of obstacle.
But the woman was given the two wings of the great eagle.

The woman did not fall into Satan's hands, it says. She fled into the wilderness on the two wings she was given. By the two wings he means revelations from the angels. One told the Magi not to go back to Herod. The other said, "Flee to Egypt and stay there." Egypt was a wilderness as far as godliness was concerned. This is indeed a paradox: that the divine was raised among the ungodly. But this happened entirely through the fatherly help of the Father in heaven, to bring them to knowledge [?], for he knows how to make better things strong even out of worse. The wilderness was Egypt, and it was also empty of Herod's authority. The wilderness is also called the mother's place, because it suitably gave her a place where she would not be disturbed. "A time, and times, and half a time" refers to the stay in the wilderness. It adds up to three and a half years, the part of Herod's life during which he began raging to destroy Christ.
Then the serpent poured from his mouth.

The serpent failed in his plot against the Virgin. So he staged for us a new drama against the Virgin and her son, meaning the events of the cross. Through these he tried to plant unbelief in the mother because of the passion, and to bring destruction on the son. By the river the serpent poured from his mouth he means the temptations, since Scripture usually uses water and rivers as allegories for them. In one place it does so through Jonah, saying, "You cast me into the deep, into the heart of the sea, and rivers surrounded me." In another it does so through the parable of the Lord himself, who says, "The rain came down, and the rivers rose, and the winds blew, and they could not throw down the house built on the rock." So the river he speaks of is the temptation that came on the mother at the Lord's passion. The elder Simeon also spoke of it to the Virgin: "And a sword will pierce your own soul too." The reason was to show that she truly went through labor and gave birth, and not merely in appearance. That is why she suffered what real mothers suffer, grieving over her child. This is how "so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed" should be understood.
From his mouth.

That is, the evil demon sent the temptations at his own command. "To sweep her away with the flood" means to drown her. For living creatures are carried and swept along by rivers when they are drowned.
But the earth came to the woman's help.

The earth swallowing the river shows that it received the Lord in death, through the tomb. He called him a river because he was full of temptations, for whose sake he endured death and burial. He is also a river of peace, which is why the prophet says, "like a river of peace." For according to the divine Paul, he is our peace, "who made the two one and broke down the dividing wall of hostility." The earth swallowed him and then gave him back again, for he came back to life on the third day, trampling down death. As the divinely inspired Peter says, "it was not possible for the Author of life to be held by it." This passage should be read with a full stop after "the earth came to the woman's help." Then, as if someone asked, "How did it help?", the answer follows: "The earth swallowed the river that the dragon had poured from his mouth." When this happened, it provoked the dragon's anger, and the dragon devised another war in turn. But someone will say: it is reasonable to take the earth's swallowing of the river as the Lord's death and burial, but where does the resurrection come from? The Apocalypse does not say that after [?] the earth vomited it up, meaning the temptation. Only that would rightly explain the dragon's anger. The swallowing would rather have added to his pleasure, since it ended more completely in the disappearance of the one who was [?]. Our answer is this. Although the words "vomited up" or "spewed out" are not added, the dragon's anger itself shows that the earth spewed it out again. This was how what provoked his anger was to come into being once more. The war is against those who are called sons and brothers of Christ, in the sense of the saying, "I will declare your name to my brothers," and again, "Here am I and the children the Lord has given me." In his anger he decided to make war on these faithful of the Lord. Through sincere faith in him and devotion to him they have been taken up into kinship with him, as we can hear him say: "These are my mother and my brothers, those who do the will of my Father in heaven."

The one who gives the revelation to the Apostle presents these things dramatically, bringing in the earth as a living creature with a mouth that opens and makes things vanish by swallowing them. It makes them vanish by swallowing through the humility of those whom the temptations attack. These people say, and believe, that they are earth and ashes. By this humility they make the arrogant height of the devil who wars against them vanish, and they bring it down, as if by a kind of swallowing. This is what the angel told Antony. The dragon was enraged at the woman, that is, the Church, because his schemes had been overthrown by humility. So he went off to make war on the rest, those of the apostolic succession. These men sprang from her seed and hold the testimony of Jesus Christ. That is, he went off to make war through the distinguished teachers of the Church and those who scorn earthly things and move to the wilderness and its hardships. If, it says, the devil fails against these because humility swallows him up, he will turn against those who serve as Christ's soldiers in the world. He hopes to find them easy to grip because of the business of life, as dust roughens a wrestler's oil and takes away its slipperiness, and so to rout them. Yet many of them, because of the genuineness of their love for Christ, mock him as if he were a feeble sparrow.
On the beast with ten horns and seven heads, one of which he said seemed to have been slaughtered.

And I stood on the sand of the sea, and I saw a beast rising out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads, and on its horns ten diadems, and on its heads names of blasphemy. And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like a bear's, and its mouth like a lion's mouth; and the dragon gave it his power and his throne and great authority.

The standing on the sand is meant to show that the things revealed are not fixed, since they are symbolic, and do not rest [?] on the very things spoken of. In the vision before this one a fiery-red dragon is seen in heaven, but now a beast is seen rising out of the sea. The dragon from heaven signifies the one who fell at the beginning from heavenly glory. The present one, in turn, rising out of the sea, presents the sea as this unstable and ever-troubled life. The beast rises out of it and takes on visible form from the faulty deeds of human beings, who are unsteady in what is good. It is none other than the Antichrist, who comes forth third, after the first and the second Satan. The second and middle one, which is now set before us for contemplation, is a certain power that fell together with the apostate Satan. It is lesser than he, but it surpasses the rest in wickedness. This is the Antichrist, put forward by the working of Satan and of the demonic powers cast down with him, if we are to trust Methodius and Hippolytus and the holy fathers. Scripture does say that Satan dwells in the sea and in Tartarus, but it says so figuratively, for in the book of Job one can hear him saying to God, "I have come, having walked about the earth and all that is under heaven." From this it is clear that he busies himself with the creation around the earth and conducts himself treacherously toward human beings. Against some he plots like a chilly Tartarus, trying to quench the warmth that is in human beings. At other times he goes forth in the manner of the sea, instils fear by the ebb and flow of worldly circumstances, and seizes people and holds them in subjection. But if he lived unseen in the sea, how is it recorded in the preceding vision that he contrived many things against the Lord and against his mother? This one, then, now set before us for contemplation, has already been called the Antichrist, who acts by the working of Satan, and Satan does not fail to cherish him as [?]. For those who are deemed worthy of special care receive the name in an intimate sense. So Christ too says to the murderous Hebrews, "You are of the father the devil," calling Satan's fellow apostate the father of the devil, as has already been said. By his working the Antichrist comes, just as Abraham too is recorded as the father of many nations, that is, of all those who in emulation of him [?] their own inborn error and laid claim to godliness. It should be known, however, that some have punctuated the Gospel saying "You are of the father the devil" differently, and they resolve the difficulty by reading the saying as ironic. When the Hebrews said, "We were not born of fornication; we have God as our father," Christ answered them mockingly, saying with ironic delivery, "You, of the Father? You are of the devil." That is: are you of God the Father, from whom every fatherhood is named? Not at all. You are not of the one who is truly Father, just as you are not truly Abraham's either: you are his by descent, but not by his God-fearing ways [?]. Descent is shared by the other living creatures too, but godliness belongs only to those who are truly wise. So much for this. He says that this beast rises out of the sea because, when the world is in extreme turmoil through wickedness, the Antichrist will be readily accepted by human beings. The ten horns indicate that the Antichrist will possess the full measure of everything that contributes to wickedness, and glory will attend him as a result, for the horn customarily signifies glory. On the basis of these horns some have also said that the inhabited world will then be divided into ten kingdoms. The seven heads signify that the kingdoms exist in this world, which corresponds to the number seven. Because it is perceptible to the senses, this world is dissolved together with life in the flesh, and then the incorruptible and everlasting world dawns, in which the kingdom also is everlasting and has no successor.
And the beast that I saw was like a leopard.
This means either that he is given to blasphemies from the very beginning, or that by blaspheming God he heaps up evil on his own head.

The names of blasphemy are on the heads of the beast that rises, and the beast is the Antichrist. Blasphemous titles will belong to him, he says. What does he mean by this? He means the beast that comes out of the sea, that is, out of this turbulent and storm-tossed life. For the Antichrist will be a man, and his forerunners will have been the pagan rulers and indeed the rulers after Constantine the Great, among whom are Julian and Valens and all the heretical emperors who followed. Then he himself will appear, once the Roman dominion has been divided into ten a little before his coming, and once the faith of the Christians has been blasphemed enough. Those who wish can learn this from the books that record ancient history and those that record recent events. The numbers ten and seven have already been discussed. As for what kind of beast it is, he says it is like a leopard, its feet like a bear's, and its mouth like a lion's. By the leopard he signifies the dominion of the Romans, which is swift to act against whomever it attacks and persists until it brings what it has begun to completion. He shows this persistence also through the bear's feet. The feet are also taken to refer to the kingdom of the Persians, which to this day has not given up holding out altogether. By the mouth he signifies the kingdom of the Babylonians, which one might reasonably take to be that of the Saracens, since their seat of government is now in Babylon. The Antichrist will rule over them as king of the Romans. He will come to this in order to destroy this kingdom too, when he sees the clay toes of the feet. These show the division of the empire into ten weak and easily crumbled dominions. These, and the Antichrist himself, the [stone?] will strike: the one who took on human existence without the cooperation of a man, came forth from the Father's divine height, and became what we are, living with us. He struck the kingdoms and ground them completely to pieces, as [chaff] from a summer threshing floor [?], and consigned the Antichrist himself to everlasting bonds. He himself has taken on immortal and indissoluble power.
And the dragon gave it his power.

Satan, the spiritual dragon, will give the Antichrist all authority in signs and wonders, though false ones, to deceive the unstable. What should we understand by the throne, if not the authority of the darkness of this air, which Satan himself obtained when he fell from heavenly glory?

And I saw one of its heads as if it had been slain to death, and its mortal wound was healed, and the whole earth marveled and followed after the beast. And they worshiped the dragon, who had given authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast? Who is able to make war with it?" And it was given a mouth speaking great things and blasphemy, and it was given authority to wage war for forty-two months. And it opened its mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name and his tabernacle and those who dwell in heaven. And it was allowed to make war with the saints and to conquer them.

This must be understood in different ways. One interpretation concerns Israel, which was a God-fearing nation. Descended from such fathers, it [went down] into Egypt on account of the famine [?], together with its father Jacob. For a certain time, while the forefathers were alive and present [?], they held to their ancestral godliness. But once those forefathers had died and their descendants had abandoned the godliness of their fathers, they were drawn into Egyptian idolatries, for which they are reproached by Joshua son of Nun in the book that bears his name. Moses estranged them from this idol-madness and from Egypt, and they were led back again to godliness. This is what he calls the slaying of one of the heads. The heads are the nations led astray by Satan himself, and bringing them over to godliness was regarded as a slaying to death. The text shows that this is not properly a slaying but is equivalent to one, for it says not "slain" but "as if slain," using "as," the particle of likeness. After this return to the knowledge of God, their running back again to their original ungodliness is called the healing of the wound. That wound, which was virtually his destruction, is our saving turn to God. Someone might cavil at this interpretation of the text, arguing that these things happened long ago, whereas the Revelation discloses things to come and not things that have already happened. Let him hear this: intervals of time are reliable when the matter concerns things that pass away. But when it concerns eternal things that never cease from their activity, where past events come to life again through their likeness to things that are accomplished once more, there will be no firm ground for rejecting what has been proposed. This, then, is one interpretation of the text, but there is another. The head as if slain may mean that one of the Antichrist's rulers will be put to death and will seem to be raised by him through deceptive sorcery, just as Simon did such things and was refuted by Peter, the chief of the apostles. Or it may mean that the dominion of the Romans, destroyed by its division into many parts, will be regarded as a kind of slaying. When the Antichrist himself puts an end to these divisions, this ending will be reckoned a healing, after the pattern of Augustus Caesar. He stripped Lepidus and Antony of their power and brought the state round to monarchy, and his preservation of the monarchy made him shine with everlasting glory.
And the whole earth marveled and followed after the beast.

That is, it was filled with amazement, as though the beast led the way with its wonders and people followed behind in assent, because they lack the habit of distinguishing truth from falsehood. "The whole earth" is said instead of "every human being," by the figure of metonymy, which names the container for what it contains, as in "the whole earth was having breakfast."
And they worshiped the dragon.

The wonder worked by the Antichrist will be referred to the devil, who works through him, for it is through the Antichrist that the dragon will be worshiped. This is why I say that the worship belongs to the dragon: it passes from the wonders the Antichrist performs to the one who works through him. After mentioning the worship of the dragon, he went on without marking any distinction. He did not add, "and after worshiping the dragon they also worshiped the beast," but spoke as though the worship of the dragon and of the beast were one and the same. The dragon did not receive this worship in person, being present only through his working. So, as though to clarify how he was worshiped, he adds, "and they worshiped the beast." The worship of the dragon has its occasion there: it is not offered to him in person, as has been said, but passes from the one who serves as its instrument to the one who is its cause.
Who is like the beast?
Who is like the beast and able to make war with it? These are the words of people who are raving and whose human reasoning has been corrupted.
And it was given a mouth speaking great things and blasphemy.

"Was given" can be taken in two ways. It may refer to God's inexpressible forbearance. Of this we grasp only that he tolerates such things in order to exercise and test our disposition toward him. Or "was given" may mean given by the deceived people who worshiped the beast. "Speaks great things" means uttering words full of arrogance. No other form of wickedness rivals arrogance, which is why Solomon says in Proverbs, "The Lord [opposes] the proud [?]..." [?] since no one but God alone is able to stand against it. Blasphemy follows the grandiose speech that is built up from excessive arrogance, and it advances unsparingly against everything. This is why David says of such people, "They have set their mouth against heaven, and their tongue has gone through the earth." Isaiah too [shows] that arrogance cannot be compared with any other evil, and that it therefore advances against God without restraint. The arrogant one is none other than this apostate, veiled under the figure of Sennacherib, in the passage where he says, "I will ascend to heaven; above the stars of heaven I will set my throne, and I will be like the Most High." How could a mortal nature say such things, bound up as it is with corruption and suffering change in its very life? So too the prophet Isaiah portrayed the Antichrist's loud-voiced blasphemy under the figure of the Assyrian and attributed these blasphemies to him. It follows that, with God's help, we should also take up what comes next in the passage set before us, which runs as follows.
To blaspheme his name.

By divine forbearance, as we have said before [?], he will have licence for three and a half years to blaspheme God and the heavenly ones. These he also calls the tabernacle, meaning either the holy angels or those who lead their lives in imitation of the angels, in keeping with the saying, "I will dwell among them." The tabernacle of God is also the incarnation of God the Word in the flesh. Against all of these he will turn his blasphemy. As for the war against the saints and his victory over them, "saints" here must be understood to mean all who have been called. So it is also said in the Old Testament that the destroyer begins with the saints. But since, according to the Lord's word, "many are called, but few are chosen," those who are conquered are likely to be those not counted among the few. Their calling did not reach the depths of their hearts. It touched them only on the surface, just enough for them to be counted among Christians.

And it was given authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation, and all who dwell on the earth will worship it, everyone whose name has not been written in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world. If anyone has an ear, let him hear. If anyone gathers others into captivity, into captivity he goes. If anyone kills with the sword, with the sword he must be killed. Here is the endurance and the faith of the saints.

It was said earlier that the time of the Antichrist's presence and of his deceitful authority will be completed in three and a half years, for this is the span of time that the forty-two months add up to.
And it was given authority over every tribe.

To leave him without excuse, he is permitted to exercise authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation, so that he cannot plead, "If I had tested these, I would have won." He made the same bold claim in Job's case when he said, "You have fenced him about, inside and out," and he was then allowed to treat everything belonging to the righteous man entirely as he pleased. Even so, he missed his aim. Tribe, people, tongue and nation differ as follows. A tribe is a clan, that is, a kinship group, set apart by its distinctness from the mixed crowd, which he calls a people. Tongue and nation are distinguished in that a nation is not defined by the way it speaks, for nothing prevents men of different nations from using one spoken language. For this reason he is precise about the multitude placed under the beast's authority and lists comprehensively everything that usually marks a difference, so that no one might suppose any part of the human race was exempt from his authority.
And all who dwell on the earth will worship it.

The word "all" carries an inclusive sense, and here too it might be taken to mean that the whole human race will worship the Antichrist. To prevent this, he gave a mark by which to identify those who worship him: he says that it is those who dwell on the earth who will worship. Isaiah too sings that these will fall. He does not say "we shall fall" but "those who dwell on the earth shall fall," meaning those who have given no thought to heavenly things and the glory there and have made themselves at home at the earthly hearth and in the swinish life that goes with it. That is why they have also failed to be enrolled in the book of life.
Of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world.

The phrase "whose names have not been written in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain" must be understood as a hyperbaton, for the names of those that have been written were written from the foundation of the world. It must be understood this way, and not in the order the text runs, because the slaying of the Lamb did not take place from the foundation of the world. And whose names were written in the Lamb's book, since they did not worship the dragon? From the nations, for example, Job and his four friends; and from Israel, the holy prophets and all those in the Old Testament who were attested for their godliness. Luke says in the Gospel that the Lord Jesus Christ also mentioned this book, when he says, "Rejoice that your names have been written in heaven."
If anyone has an ear, let him hear.

"If anyone has an ear," he says, directing the meaning conveyed by the words to the governing mind. Let such a person hear what has been said, and know that whoever is quick to take others captive will receive the wages of what he has done. This is what "goes into captivity" is meant to convey. The verb can also mean "brings under," that is, "subjects," as of those whom he brings into captivity. But the point is that he himself will be taken captive by the beast and will receive no rescue from God to keep him from being led away. If anyone is murderous by character, he too will be killed by Satan with the spiritual death of the soul, through worshiping him. Such people were defeated through their deeds, busying themselves with abductions and murders to please the adversary. Having been enslaved to him, they will bear the hardships of slavery. Here the endurance of the godly is seen: they do not give in because of the afflictions that Satan brings upon them. For this they will be rewarded on the basis of their faith as saints, since they too accomplished everything praiseworthy by faith, if we are to believe Paul, who explains this to the Hebrews. These things have been set out more fully to clarify the concise text.
For by endurance the souls are gained, that is, saved, as one can hear from the Lord himself, who says, "By your endurance gain your souls."
Concerning another beast, which has two horns and brings people to the first beast.

And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon. And it exercises all the authority of the first beast before it. And it made the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose mortal wound had been healed. And it performs great signs, even making fire come down from heaven to the earth in the sight of people. And it deceives my own, those who dwell on the earth, by the signs that it was given to perform before the beast.

After many digressions from these starting points, and after going back to still earlier ones, he has arrived at the matter in hand. This is nothing other than to relate what concerns the coming of the Antichrist. And see what he says about him: that he comes up from the earth, the source from which all human beings come into being. For he too is a man, acting by the working of Satan, as the divine Paul also holds. His horns are not a lamb's but like a lamb's, because he makes himself appear gentle like Christ in order to deceive. That is the reason for the likeness of the horns, that is, of the glory. And he speaks like a dragon, though he is not a dragon. For he is not Satan himself, but he wields authority as Satan does; that is, he becomes the successor to the devil's authority. "Before him" means, as it were, in conformity with him, closely following him, differing in nothing [?] from the presence of the first, Satan. In this way he also prepares all those who care for nothing beyond earthly things, and who share their way of life along with their dwelling on earth, to worship the first beast. But how can this be, since the devil cannot appear to the senses so that the worship might be plainly directed to him? It is not openly directed to him. But, as has already been said, the worship offered to the Antichrist through Satan's cooperation passes over to the cooperator himself. The deeds of those who work together with someone are not credited to the ones through whom the work is done. They are credited to the one who displays his own work through them as through an instrument. To see that this is so, hear what Paul says. After wrestling with many hardships, he ascribes the victory not to himself but to the one who loved him: "In all these things," he says, "we more than conquer through him who loved us." He says the same when he declares, "Yet not I, but the grace of God that is with me." Moreover, the Antichrist exercises all authority before the beast while Satan is not visibly present. To explain this, it is enough to cite what the Lord said to God the Father about his disciples: "Yes, Father, for such was your good pleasure before you." This shows that whatever is done to please someone is reckoned as done before the one who is pleased, even when he is not present.
That is: following close behind, preparing the way for the worship of the first beast.
Whose mortal wound had been healed.

This was discussed more fully earlier. Here he has indicated only as much as is needed to make the point. He said that this beast exercises all the authority of the first beast before it. But first of all he had spoken of the red dragon, which the vision showed depicted in heaven. So, lest anyone think that he is now speaking of that dragon when he mentions the authority of the first beast, he says: I do not mean that first one. I mean the one after him and before the Antichrist, whom the vision showed coming up out of the sea, like a leopard. For it was this beast's wound that was healed, as was said earlier. For he says that this one performs signs and wonders by the working of the devil, as the divine Paul also holds, as we have already said. The signs are the bringing down of fire from heaven, as also happened in the case of Job, when the devil used it to destroy the righteous man's livestock. There are other such great signs as well, so great that they astound and capture even those who already believe. This is what he means by saying "he deceives my own," just as Christ says in the Gospel: "so as to deceive, if possible, even the elect." And to show which of Christ's faithful he will deceive, he added their distinguishing mark, "those who dwell on the earth." He does not say this to distinguish angels from human beings. For which of the angels could they deceive? Their natural purity allows nothing to stand in the way and hide the truth from them. No, he will astound those people on earth whose dwelling-place shows what their mind is set on. They have nothing lofty about them, no godly and heavenly thought. Their whole concern is to wallow like cattle in the earth and earthly things.
In the sight of people.

He performs great signs by tricking the eyes of those who watch. So did the Egyptian sorcerers before Pharaoh, and Simon Magus in Rome when he raised the dead man, though he was exposed by Peter. So, he says, the forerunner of the Antichrist will do everything by sorcery. His aim is that the Antichrist may be thought to be Christ, since such a wonder-worker bears witness to him and he receives unquestioned glory. This imitates John the Baptist, who bore witness to Christ the Savior and went before him. For falsehood is terribly skilled at imitating the truth by deceit, to the ruin of those who are persuaded.
It was given to him to perform before the beast.

"Before" can mean "in the presence of." It can also mean "in a manner worthy of" and "in keeping with." This is its sense in "to serve him in holiness and righteousness before him": here we are to serve him in a manner worthy of the divine holiness and righteousness. So here too "before" is to be understood in this way. The meaning is that the signs he was permitted to perform belonged not to truth but to deceit, as befits the deceiver who works them.

…telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image of the beast that had the wound of the sword and lived. And it was given to him to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast should even speak, and should cause those who would not worship the image of the beast to be killed. And he causes all, the small and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the slaves, to be given marks on their right hand or on their forehead, so that no one can buy or sell unless he has the mark.

The command is given with great precision to those who dwell on the earth. Isaiah says in his song that these people are persuaded, "We shall not fall"; but "those who dwell on the earth shall fall." It is to these, then, and not to those whose citizenship is in heaven, that the making of the image is now commanded. For there is no chance that the latter will be deceived, since they have been carefully safeguarded by the advance announcement of the beast's coming. The warning "If anyone has an ear, let him hear" was set down earlier concerning the beast that had the wound and lived.

And since an image of the beast was also set up, it was also given to him to give breath to the image, so that the image might seem to speak. This should be compared with the statues, many of which are recorded to have sweated and spoken in pagan times through the devil's working. The construction of the passage is as follows. The word "that" is to be taken as governing each clause, so that it reads: that it might both speak and cause that whoever does not worship the image of the beast should be killed. That statues spoke, as has been said, may be learned from history, just as trees and waters too are recorded to have spoken through sorcery, by Apollonius and other sorcerers. Simon Magus, too, made a show of raising a dead man in Peter's presence, as we said earlier. Peter exposed the raising as an illusion, for he himself did away with the deception by a true raising.

Thus the shield-bearer of the Antichrist, after laboring [?] at his deceptive illusions, will order an image of the beast to be made and display it. He will also arrange for those who do not worship it to be killed.
And he causes all, the small and the great, and so on.

The construction is rather colloquial and so makes no sense. Does he mean that the small and the great receive the marks, or give them? So by adding the preposition "to" the sense could be set right, as follows: "and he causes, to all the small and the great and the rest, that they give them marks on the right hand or on the forehead." He says this serves as a sign of who may trade and who may not. Here too the conjunction "and" is redundant, I mean in "and that no one can buy or sell." The conjunction "and" is superfluous, for there is neither a cancellation nor a shift from the preceding thought, which is what this conjunction naturally signals. Rather, the causal conjunction gives the reason for what was said above about the giving of the mark, namely why the mark was given. It was given so that no one would be allowed to carry on trade without this means of recognition.
On their right hand.

The mark is on the right hand and on the forehead. For the engraving of the destructive name is the counterpart of the mark of the good. It is on the right hands, to cut off the working of good deeds. It is on the foreheads, so that by seizing the part that lies above the eyes it may bring darkness upon the deceived. Then they cannot hold fast to piety decently, as in the daylight. But those whose faces have been marked with the divine light of the countenance will not receive it.
On the name of the beast.
…either the name of the beast or the number of its name. Here is wisdom. Let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast; for it is a human number, and its number is 666.

And he adds what the mark is: the name of the beast. It can be recognized in two ways, either by pronouncing the name itself or by its numerical value. He will take pains to spread the number of the beast's name everywhere, in selling and buying, so that whoever does not bear it may die for lack of necessities. The name is called a human number, meaning that it is not foreign, unusual, hidden or ambiguous. It is a number that is familiar and well known to people. The number of the name's value is 666. He did not state the name itself plainly, for one of two reasons. Perhaps it was unworthy to be written in a book. Or perhaps, since it is not made plain, many evildoers would not be able to claim it for themselves. They would trouble the pious by snatching in advance at knowledge of his coming, and by fixing its fulfillment at the wrong moment they would miss the right time altogether. So, for the sake of exercise, it is not out of place to collect names that yield this number, both proper names and common nouns. Proper names include Lampetis and Teitan, spelled with the diphthong because it comes from the future tense teno, just as sporos comes from spero. Lateinos is likewise spelled with the diphthong. Then there is Benediktos, which is more fitting than these. Explained from the language of the Italians it means "blessed," and so it will appeal to the apostate, since it has also been applied to the true Christ. Common nouns include ho nikētēs, "the victor," for perhaps he will call himself this. Others are kakos hodēgos, "evil guide," alēthēs blaberos, "truly harmful," palai baskanos, "envious of old," and amnos adikos, "unjust lamb." These are what his opponents will call him, and he will reap his own glory in shame.

From the works of Andrew. Time and experience will reveal the exact calculation of the number to those who are watchful, as they will the other things written about him.
